searchText: while waiting for some better place to discuss subroutines.. I'm analyzing the mainnet code now a bit. <@!425279588009246720> , example of code which contains both JUMP/JUMPI and BEGINSUB: ```  ``` (edited with better example) Do you know what that code is all about? Is that the solidity signature at the end? It is. We have run a similar check with <@!259648573401071617> and agreed we need to extend the code analysis tool to avoid these cases 🙂 The Solidity metadata is at the end, but is demarcated with a STOP opcode. <@!291925846556540928> could you create an #evm channel for us (under eth1x)? or you can just rename this one I think merklization is a different context we wanted to discuss under "evm". We wish to discuss any proposed EIP, etc. I just thought that when we have something to discuss in merkelisation, we create a new channel for it 🙂 And not particularly linked to eth1x, just to eth1 in general. `00a165627a7a72305820fcb224e7d7358adb2c278cc3750c559920b3c5f2ac8eaebe55ab9e79486ecdd60029` Is the end of your snippet. The first `00` is the stop. The rest is CBOR encoded mapping. The very last 2 bytes are big-endian encoded length of the CBOR, excluding this length field. I'm doing a variant which seems more promising now.. Where I only check if a `JUMPDEST` is located _after_ a `BEGINSUB`. Found `154` occurrences so far -- the one I looked at looks like pure 'data' not evm code You are only looking at deployed code and not constructor code, right? <#706868829900505180> created! Only deployed code, at block `9666637` Ok, let's scoot over to the `evm` channel I guess ?
